items_missed: No agenda statement — never framed what the call would cover or how long it would take, so the customer set the direction instead of the rep
No move-date availability check at any point in the call
No recap of the details on the quote form — rep did not have the file in front of him, guessed the prior rep was 'Zach' after the customer said 'Dylan or Dustin'

Essentially zero discovery: no origin/destination address or zip, no stairs or floors, no garage/storage/balcony rooms, no packing needs, no box count, no additional stops, no access or parking concerns, no moving stressors question

Customer volunteered that this was his first call and he had no idea what local rates were — a wide-open door to differentiate, and the rep gave no differentiators at all (no No Worries Damage Coverage, no Meet Your Mover, no On-Time Guarantee, no 'no hidden fees')
Virtual walkthrough was floated but never actually booked — no specific day/time offered, and after the customer deferred the rep dropped it entirely instead of re-attempting
No 'no deposit required' mention, which is the single strongest thing to say to a customer who is actively price-shopping
Confirmation email described only as 'basic pricing info' — no bolded-details list and no 'reply with any corrections'
No 'any other questions before I let you go?' close
No hours or specific contact instructions — only a vague 'reach out to us'
top_strength: Erik handled an awkward duplicate-lead situation with real grace — he acknowledged the possible double-contact, explicitly protected the other rep ('I'll just reach out to him and make sure he gets that over to you'), and the customer ended the call volunteering praise for how thorough Einstein is. He also proactively suggested checking the spam folder before assuming the estimate was never sent.
coaching_note: The customer handed Erik the best possible opening and he walked past it: 'he was my first phone call... not really familiar with current rates... I was anticipating calling other moving companies.' That is a price-shopper telling you he has no basis for comparison yet. That is the moment to run the differentiator block — No Worries Damage Coverage up to $2,000, Meet Your Mover, the On-Time Guarantee, and no deposit / no hidden fees — so that when he calls the next three companies he is measuring them against Einstein instead of measuring Einstein against a $101/hr number. Erik also needed to close the virtual walkthrough with a specific time ('I have Tuesday at 2 or Wednesday at 10 — which is easier?') rather than leaving it as 'reach out whenever.' Discovery being near-zero is a second issue, but the differentiator miss on a self-identified comparison shopper is the one that cost the booking.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently warm and natural — 'Totally understand, sir, 100 percent', a light joke that landed, and the customer reciprocated with unprompted praise; held back from a 5 only by a disorganized, disfluent stretch mid-call where he audibly lost the thread.
